description.ja: Autona のプラグイン契約 1（ADR-009 D8）。Worker Protocol 1・マニフェスト 1・入力源の format 1・プラグインの v1 ルートの区分の機械可読の正本。plugin.schema.json（マニフェストの JSON Schema）・routes_v1.json（ルート表）・inputs/（入力源の golden）と一緒に読む。tests/test_plugin_contract.py がこれらの自己整合と src/core/PluginTypes.py の列挙との一致を、後の段階のテストが実エンジン・SDK の偽ホスト・偽ワーカーとの一致を確かめる。上げる条件は ADR-009 D8（項目の削除・意味の変更・必須の追加で版を上げ、イベント・任意項目・型・契機・欄の追加では上げない）。プレビュー中は壊す変更もありうる（CHANGELOG とカードで知らせる）。
description.en: Autona plugin contract 1 (ADR-009 D8): the machine-readable source of truth for Worker Protocol 1, manifest 1, input format 1 and the access classes of the plugin v1 routes. Read with plugin.schema.json (the manifest's JSON Schema), routes_v1.json (the route table) and inputs/ (the input sources' golden files). tests/test_plugin_contract.py holds these to each other and to the enums of src/core/PluginTypes.py; later stages' tests hold the real engine, the SDK's fake host and the fake worker to it. Versions go up as ADR-009 D8 says (a removal, a change of meaning or a new required item; not an added event, optional item, type, trigger or field). While in preview a breaking change can still happen (announced in the CHANGELOG and on the plugin's card).

patterns.name: ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$
patterns.name_note: A field type, a hook's on, an action's target in a manifest: an open name. Only the values this contract lists are known; another one makes the job (in settings: the plugin) unusable, never the manifest (D8).
patterns.dev_folder_id_format: the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 (UTF-8) of os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(folder)): stable across launches and list changes
patterns.run_id_format: <local YYYYMMDD>-<local HHMMSS>-<4 of [a-z0-9]> (ArchiveJobService.JOB_ID_PATTERN; the job folder's name)

text.description: A text (文言) is a string, or an object of locale -> string with at least one entry. The host shows: the current locale, then en, then ja, then the first value. A length limit on a text applies to each value.

describe.expected: one stdout line (the answer), exit 0; other lines are ignored
describe.runner_note: PluginRunner.Describe runs it and reports these facts only (DescribeRun: objects are the JSON-object lines in order). PluginRegistry judges them against the manifest (JudgeDescribe) and owns every unusable_when code.
describe.note: The first stdout line that is a JSON object with type describe is the answer; other lines are ignored. no_line: no non-empty stdout line; not_json: no JSON-object line; type_not_describe: JSON objects but none with type describe. The events' rules (ignored_keys, raw) do not apply to describe. Never called before consent; never called for a blocked plugin; the result is not cached.

entry.installed: argv; entry[0] is a relative path inside the plugin folder (no absolute path, no drive, no '..', no leading '@'), a file ending in .exe that exists; no shell
entry.dev: entry[0] may also be any command found on PATH (python, node) or a relative path; no shell

events.line: one JSON object per stdout line, UTF-8, flushed per line; read with errors=replace
events.ignored_note: id is reserved for a future two-way protocol: the key is ignored and the line taken as its type says.
events.raw: Every taken event keeps the line's whole object as raw (unknown keys included), and the run's outcome keeps the last terminal line's (final_raw): a built-in worker's own fields (vodsplit's done: sets, needs_review, clips, skipped, template ...) are read from it. raw is not a protocol key.
events.invalid_field: dropped (the event is still taken; a terminal event stays terminal)

types.host: starts a new stage; the stage name is not interpreted
kept on the job, the first max_warnings of them
terminal: success when the exit code is 0
terminal: a failure the user can fix when the exit code is 2. message and hint must hold no secret

over_limit.warnings: the ones past max_warnings are dropped
over_limit.artifacts: the ones past max_artifacts are dropped with a host warning
over_limit.error_code: a code not matching the pattern becomes 'error'

kinds.display: full text with a copy button; never rendered as HTML
scaled preview (fetched into a blob URL)

artifacts.rejected_note: A rejected artifact is dropped and a host warning is added to the job. An image over max_bytes or with another extension is rejected; a text over max_bytes is rejected. Served with a fixed Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, on SHELL routes only.
artifacts.hook_runs: a hook's job folder is removed when it ends (but the last failed one): no artifact is kept, the history keeps the summary. A dev plugin's sample run (PluginHooks.TrySample) is kept like a manual run (its folder and artifacts; counted in runs_kept_per_plugin; not in the runs list, read by its run_id)

checked_first.note: the process could not be created and there is no exit code. reason entry_missing when the entry file is not there (the hint mentions antivirus quarantine)
the host's mark; whatever the terminal line and exit code, even done with exit 0

end.table_note: The same order as ArchiveJobService._EndState: (exit 0 and done) -> (exit 130 or cancelled) -> (exit 2 and error) -> (cancel requested and no terminal line) -> failed. after_cancel_request applies only to the rows that carry it.
end.done_after_cancel_request: state done with finished_before_cancel true (the page adds 'it had finished before the cancel')

failed_reasons.memory_limit: a failed light-lane run whose PeakJobMemoryUsed reached its memory limit
failed_reasons.autona_exited: a generic run still running in job.json at launch (no resume: failed, not cancelled)

stdin.after_grace: kill the job object (the run and every descendant in it)

limits.display_truncation_note: The host's own limits (not ADR-009's): a longer text (each value of a locale map) is truncated where it is shown or kept. Never a reason to refuse an event, a field or a manifest.
limits.heavy_memory: no limit; the declared memory_mb is recorded only; the peak is recorded and listed

lanes.heavy: vodsplit and lane heavy jobs, manual only
lanes.light: lane light jobs: manual, actions and hooks
lanes.busy: a manual or action request to a full lane is refused with reason busy (and the remaining time); no queue, no automatic retry
lanes.hook_pending: a hook trigger to a full light lane is held (latest one per hook); when the lane frees, a user's request goes before a pending hook

key.unique: within a job's params, within settings

value.stored: the absolute path the host resolved the pick id to
value.shown: the file name only (GET answers the name, never the path)

value.stored: the absolute path the host resolved the pick id to
value.shown: the folder name only (GET answers the name, never the path)

value.value: string of 1 to 4096 characters with no line break, NUL or other control character (Unicode category Cc); another, or an empty one, is refused (invalid_request; DELETE clears it)
value.passed: environment variable AUTONA_SECRET_<KEY in upper case> only; never in request.json, job.json or a log

source.content: match log lines (JSONL), as MatchLogService writes them (split on line feeds only); a line that is not a JSON object -- one a crash cut short -- is dropped
source.manual: pick a date and a tournament
source.choice_id: YYYYMMDD (the whole day) or YYYYMMDD/<tournament> (that day's records whose tournament is exactly it; an empty one: the records with none)
source.at_trigger: the log file of the open record's start date (today's when no record is open), every line that is a JSON object (an empty file when none); the host flushes MatchLogService's writer (Flush) before copying
source.at_trigger_known_limit: records started on an earlier date (a session past midnight) are in that date's file and are not included

source.content: one match record (one line of the log, as one JSON object)
a copy of the published state (the shape of out/program_state.json)
source.manual: no choice: the state at the press (manual included)
source.at_trigger: the published state at the trigger

source.content: one result image (png / jpg) and its sha256
source.golden_note: a stand-in image (not a real result): the dev plugins' sample run of a result_image_saved hook (PluginHooks.TrySample)

source.content: one match thumbnail and its sha256
the list of an archive export (JSON; the clips stay where they are): an archive job's clips/export.json, the clips it marks exported and not skipped whose file is in the clips folder, in its order

shape.clips_dir: string (absolute path of the job's clips folder)
shape.clips: array of {no: integer (from 1), path: string (absolute), file: string (its file name), title: string, start: number (seconds), end: number (seconds)}

source.shape_note: The least shape (lane L3). P3 widens it against the YouTube ADR by adding fields only, during the preview (format stays 1).

fill_rules: A job with an action or a hook has exactly one field of the type that trigger fills (per trigger).
Every way a job can start fills every context-only field of the job (match_record, archive_export); a job with a context-only field has manual false.

In an action or a hook, a source field other than the filled one is filled by at_trigger (state, match_log); a result_image / thumbnail_image field it does not fill makes that trigger invalid when required, and is null when optional.
In a manual run the user picks each source field (required ones must be picked; an optional one not picked is null).
A state field is never picked: it is the published state at the press or the trigger, whatever the start.
inputs in request.json holds every source key of the job; an unfilled optional one is null.
triggers.hook_input_note: match_record from match_decided is the record's line at the moment it fires (closed false).

manifest_checks.description: What a host (PluginRegistry) and the SDK's check report about a manifest. scope: plugin = the plugin cannot be used; job = that job cannot be used (shown with the reason), the others still can; warning = shown, nothing refused. settings_scope: the scope when the problem is in settings (settings serve every job). schema: the part of plugin.schema.json that fails on it (top = the top level, settings, job = #/$defs/job), null when the schema cannot express it. owner: the part that reports it.

schema_scopes.how: Validate the manifest against the schema with every job left out (jobs only as a non-empty array of objects): a failure is invalid_field (plugin). Then validate each job against #/$defs/job: a failure is the specific job-scoped code below when the host can tell, else invalid_job_field (that job only).

codes.note: missing, over manifest_max_bytes, not UTF-8 (a BOM is accepted), not a JSON object
the top level or settings breaks the schema; also a job id used by two jobs (the schema cannot say it), and an id with a part that is a Windows device name (con, nul, aux, prn, com1-9, lpt1-9)
a job breaks #/$defs/job in a way no other code names
an unknown top-level key: ignored
the id against the folder's name, or against the id the installer expects for its <id>.new folder (Check's expectedId). Never for a dev folder: its name is free
taguyan. from anything but the official repository ids (the source passed to Check) or a dev folder
a dev folder with an installed id, or the other way round: the one added later is refused. Check alone cannot see it
platforms does not hold windows-x64 (other names beside it are fine)
entry[0] starts with @
after resolving (the schema catches the plain absolute / .. forms)
entry[0] is not there; installed: also when it is not a file ending in .exe

not a relative .png path inside the folder (checked after resolving), not a png signature, over icon_max_bytes: no icon. An icon never makes the plugin unusable, so the schema holds it to a string only
a type not in field_types (an open name in the schema)
an on not in triggers.hooks (an open name in the schema)
a target not in triggers.actions (an open name in the schema)
an action / hook without exactly one field of the type it fills
a trigger cannot fill a context-only field, or a required image field
a default not of the type (the schema catches the known types' JSON type), a select default not among the options
light only; heavy's memory_mb is recorded, never refused
manual false and no action or hook

dev_list_fields.enabled: boolean: the developer toggle (dev.json's folders are scanned only while it is true)
dev_list_fields.folders: array of absolute paths, in the order they were added

manifest_paths.dev_list_note: UTF-8 (a BOM is accepted when read), written whole. One that cannot be read is moved aside before the next write, never overwritten; until then the toggle reads off and the list empty.
manifest_paths.dev_folder_key: patterns.dev_folder_id (a folder is named by it, never by its position)

install_fields.source: object: {kind: install.source_kinds, repo_id: integer (github only), name: string owner/repo when installed (github only; display)}

manifest_paths.install_note: UTF-8 without a BOM, written by the installer only, inside the swap. One that cannot be read makes the next install of the id a new install (the safe side).
manifest_paths.listing_bundled: <Autona folder>/assets/plugins.json (the copy shipped with Autona; none in a source checkout)
manifest_paths.listing_note: The blocklist in effect is the listing copy's blocked rows, else the shipped copy's, else none (fetching plugins.json is P5b's).

enabled_fields.enabled: boolean (false: disabled; no file, or one that cannot be read, is enabled)

install.source_kinds_note: github: downloaded from the listing or an update, or a manual zip whose SHA-256 matched that repository's latest release descriptor (C.3); manual: any other zip. A dev folder and the built-in have no install.json.
install.states_note: An install (routes_v1.json InstallStatus): preparing (a job: the zip checked and expanded to .new, plugin.json read) -> consent (the sheet shown) -> installing (a job: describe in .new, the swap, install.json) -> done. failed carries the error; cancelled is a declined sheet. A consent refused because a run of the plugin goes returns to consent with the error (busy).
install.removal_states_note: A removal (routes_v1.json RemovalInfo): idle (none asked), removing (a job), failed (the last one's error). A removal that succeeded leaves the plugin gone (404).
install.errors_note: An install's or a removal's failure (routes_v1.json InstallFailure): its code (PluginInstaller's InstallError, and failed for anything unexpected) -> the refusal reason it carries. problems holds bad_zip's zip_problems, manifest_invalid's manifest check codes and describe_failed's describe failure. manifest_changed: the staged plugin.json no longer matches the consented sheet at the commit (the staged copy is discarded).
install.zip_problems_note: PluginInstaller.CheckZip's codes (C.1 / C.7): the zip's own rules first (unreadable, over zip_max_entries / zip_expanded_max_bytes, a path that escapes, a bad, non-ASCII or reserved name, a link, an encrypted entry, a name twice, the longest installed path over installed_path_max_length), then over zip_max_bytes, the release descriptor (its fields, the zip's size and SHA-256), and the layout (one <id>/ folder named a plugin id, its plugin.json readable, the id and version against the descriptor, entry[0] a file of the zip).

environment.base: the parent's environment (os.environ), minus the removed names, plus the added ones
environment.remove_note: Removed: every AUTONA_* (AUTONA_VODSPLIT_CMD, AUTONA_PLUGIN_DEV, AUTONA_INSTANCE_TAG, AUTONA_STRICT_THREAD_ASSERT, other plugins' AUTONA_SECRET_*) and QT_API, which Autona sets for itself. The added AUTONA_* below are set after the removal. Not a boundary: it keeps values from leaking by accident.

add.name: AUTONA_PLUGIN_DIR
add.value: the plugin's folder (absolute; the .new folder during an install)

add.name: AUTONA_PROTOCOL
add.value: the protocol version used, as a decimal string

add.name: AUTONA_SECRET_<KEY>
add.value: each secret setting that is set; KEY is the field key in upper case

request.writer: host; the plugin only reads it

params.note: every value field key of the job (pressed form / saved hook values; an empty optional one is its default, else null; a file / folder is the absolute path the host resolved its pick id to); {} without value fields

inputs.note: every source field key of the job -> input file or null; {} without source fields

path.note: absolute, in the job folder's inputs/

out_dir.note: absolute; made by the host before the start

data_dir.note: absolute; the plugin's small state, not encrypted, shared by its runs in both lanes

job_record.description: What PluginJobs keeps for a run (the job folder's job.json) and the SHELL route GET .../runs/<run_id> answers. No secret, no environment.

fields.artifacts: array of {path, kind, label} (the accepted ones)

plugin_list.state_precedence_note: When more than one applies, the first of this list is shown.
plugin_list.state_scope: the plugin's only: disabled is the user's disable of the plugin. A hook disabled automatically (rate_limit, failures) shows on its hook row (SHELL), never here.

refusals.description: Why a request (a start, a describe, a settings save, a dev folder, an install) is not carried out. v1 answers error.reason the code with the status of its row (409 CONFLICT unless said) and error.code that status's v1 code (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, 404 NOT_FOUND, 409 CONFLICT, 503 UNAVAILABLE); error.message is the refusal's detail (never a path, a value or a secret), for busy the remaining seconds when known (routes_v1.json envelope).

codes.note: the lane is full; carries the remaining seconds when known
a required setting (secret too) is missing; not a hook failure
a dev folder with an installed id, or an install with a dev folder's
a body that does not fit: an unknown job or key, a value of the wrong type, an unknown pick id

a desktop feature asked in the headless shell (an image input, a hook), the shell is shutting down, or the host could not write its own file (dev.json, config.json, hooks.json, a run's folder; the detail says which, never the path), or the plugin is being installed or removed (its starts are held). SHELL routes answer 403 headless before this

hooks.auto_disable_shown: on the hook's row (HookStatus: disabled_reason, last_error); never in the list's state
hooks.match_decided_candidates: MatchCandidate again for a record waiting: the line is replaced, the wait keeps counting from the first candidate. The dispatcher keeps the fired mark per record; a candidate of a fired record is ignored. MatchWithdrawn cancels the wait without marking.
hooks.disabled_reasons_note: user: the user turned it off. rate_limit, failures, params_changed: the dispatcher, for that hook only (params_changed: a saved value no longer fits the job's fields -- an update changed them -- or the start was refused invalid_request; the user confirms the values again; a refusal whose detail starts input_unavailable -- the trigger's input could not be filled -- is not one: the history says discarded / input_unavailable and the hook stays on). reconsent, new_install, blocked, removed: PluginHooks.Forget, for every hook of the plugin (reconsent and new_install put the values back to the defaults and the failures to 0; new_install also clears the history and the last error: another plugin now; removed comes before its user_data folder goes). A plugin's own disable leaves its hooks as they are: a pending one is discarded when it would start (disabled).
hooks.order: trigger -> held when the light lane is full (overwrite; when the lane frees after a manual / action start was refused busy, the pending hooks wait 5 s for that request first) -> before the start the 60 s window (skip or start) -> after the start the 1 h window (disable when over)
